# mimid — Agent Instructions

These rules apply to every agent (Claude Code via `CLAUDE.md`, Codex directly). Mark's global rules in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/standards/rust.md` also apply; this file adds only what is specific to mimid.

## Beads Issue Tracker

Use Beads (`bd`) for durable task tracking in repositories that include it. Use the `beads` skill at `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` (project install) or `~/.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` (global install) for Beads workflow guidance, then use the `bd` CLI for issue operations.

### Quick Reference

```bash
bd ready                # Find available work
bd show <id>            # View issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim work
bd close <id>           # Complete work
bd prime                # Refresh Beads context
```

### Rules

- Use `bd` for all task tracking; do not create markdown TODO lists.
- Run `bd prime` when Beads context is missing or stale. Codex 0.129.0+ can load Beads context automatically through native hooks; use `/hooks` to inspect or toggle them.
- Keep persistent project memory in Beads via `bd remember`; do not create ad hoc memory files.

**Architecture in one line:** issues are stored as flat JSON files in `.beads/issues/`, tracked by git. Sync is via standard git operations.

## What mimid is

A Rust reference implementation of IETF MIMI over MLS (RFC 9420), plus enough product around it to be a usable chat system. It implements the latest drafts as written. The spec texts are in `~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/`. Read them there, not over the network.

| Draft | Version |
|---|---|
| draft-ietf-mimi-protocol | -06 |
| draft-ietf-mimi-content | -10 |
| draft-ietf-mimi-room-policy | -04 |
| draft-ietf-mimi-arch | -03 |
| draft-ietf-mls-extensions | -10 |
| draft-ietf-mls-ratchet-tree-options | -02 |

## Settled decisions: do not relitigate

Every design decision is a closed `decision` bead under epic `mimid-1wgh`. Persistent rules are in `bd memories`. Read the relevant ones before starting work on a bead.

Known weaknesses that are deliberate: BasicCredential only, and no authentication between providers. Never describe mimid as protecting against a malicious or impersonated provider. Never claim conformance to protocol-06's mutually authenticated TLS.

## Crate map

Dependencies point down this table, never up.

| Crate | Owns | Must not |
|---|---|---|
| `mimi-mls` | All OpenMLS usage, the `wire` newtypes, label helpers | Do I/O |
| `mimi-content` | mimi-content-10 CBOR and MessageId | Depend on openmls or tokio; contain encryption (attachments are `.14`) |
| `mimi-room-policy` | room-policy-04 codecs and policy evaluation | Depend on `mimi-mls` |
| `mimi-protocol` | protocol-06 wire types and franking | Use openmls directly (MLS types come only through `mimi_mls::wire`); do I/O |
| `mimid-server` | Hub and follower roles, the provider's JMAP Chat endpoint, admin CLI | Parse or decrypt application ciphertext; put SQL outside its store module |
| `mimid-agent` | MLS keys and plaintext. It is the only component that sees either. It is the JMAP Chat ↔ MIMI bridge: users run a standard JMAP Chat client against its local endpoint | Serve plaintext anywhere except its local endpoint |

mimid ships no UI of its own (decision mimid-1wgh.38). Any standard JMAP Chat client talks plaintext JMAP Chat to the local agent.

- The spec crates (`mimi-*`) are synchronous and pure. Only the server and agent are async.
- JMAP Chat types come from `~/PROJECT/crate-jmap`. Build its `#[non_exhaustive]` types through serde, not new constructors.
- Before any write to `~/PROJECT/crate-jmap`, `~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec` or the openmls patch branch, ask Mark. Each write needs its own approval.

## Implementing specs

- Read the whole spec section before writing code. Never guess a field name.
- Give spec-check subagents both the draft section and the code file.
- Rust type and field names mirror the spec's names, so a reviewer can line the two up.
- Implement every MUST. Implement every SHOULD, unless a comment cites the section and says why not.
- Do not add fields, methods or errors the spec doesn't define, except where a decision bead labels them `INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC`.
- Every ambiguity becomes a decision bead citing the draft, the section, the competing readings, the chosen reading and why. The code carries a short pointer to it, e.g. `// mimi-content-10 §3.3; decision mimid-1wgh.<id>`. Never resolve one silently.
- If the spec looks wrong, implement it as written and file a bead labelled `wg`, so it can go back to the working group.

## Wire formats and tests

- **The fixture test direction is fixed:**
  1. Decode the fixture.
  2. Compare the result to the expected value.
  3. Re-encode it.
  4. Require byte-identical output.

  An encode-then-decode test alone proves nothing.
- **Fixtures come from outside the code under test:**
  - spec examples;
  - WG files;
  - hex encoded by hand from the TLS presentation-language text, with byte-by-byte comments;
  - output from independent implementations (plain OpenMLS, mls-rs, Python `cryptography`).

  Commit them with a `PROVENANCE` file (source, commit, SHA-256). Commit any generator script next to its output.
- **Sign and hash the exact bytes as received.** Never re-encode before verifying.
- **Decode strictly.** Reject non-canonical encodings, trailing bytes and invalid enum values.
- **Every size, depth and count limit is a named constant**, enforced at parse time. Fail closed.
- **Unknown extensions and fields round-trip unchanged.** In MLS, copy unknown GroupContext extensions through unchanged. Untrusted extensions get caps; drop a malformed or oversized one without failing the containing object.
- **Test hostile input:** values at and past every limit, deep nesting, huge arrays, invalid UTF-8, null bytes, and bidi or zero-width characters.
- **A bug fix starts with a regression test**, and that test must fail before the fix.
- **Tests are fully offline.**

## Rust conventions (in addition to rust.md)

- Put `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at every crate root.
- Library crates use `thiserror` with `#[non_exhaustive]` public enums; only binaries use `anyhow`.
- No `unwrap` or `expect` on any path a network or socket input can reach.
- A type that only a checked constructor may build (verified or authenticated messages) lives in a submodule with private fields, never at the crate root.
- Every crate's rustdoc has a `# Limitations` section.

## Security invariants

- **Authorization happens in exactly one place per boundary:**

  | Boundary | Check |
  |---|---|
  | Agent socket | Peer credentials |
  | JMAP | Bearer token |
  | Hub | Room policy |

  Each check has a test showing a wrong identity is rejected.
- **The envelope's sender must match the authenticated MLS sender**, checked before any write.
- **MLS validity alone picks the winning Commit**, and the first valid Commit per epoch in hub order wins. Room policy is checked afterwards.
- **Never delete group state because decryption fails.** Mark the group out of sync and wait.
- **Secrets never reach logs:**
  - secret-bearing types redact their `Debug` output;
  - a canary test captures `tracing` output and proves no secret appears in it;
  - never log full request bodies at INFO.
- **The agent treats everything a server or peer sends as untrusted:** it passes content to clients as data, never interprets HTML, and never lets a peer-supplied field claim another user's identity (the sender is always the authenticated MLS sender). Rendering safety (bidi isolation, no raw HTML) is the JMAP client's job.

## Agent workflow

- **One subagent per bead.** It claims the bead, stays in scope and closes it. Parallel beads each get their own git worktree. Never let two agents edit the same file.
- **Use non-interactive commands:** `cp -f`, `rm -f`, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes`.
- **Plans live in the bead's design field.** No planning, audit or scratch markdown files in the repo.
- **Break a bead into sub-issues only when it is next on the critical path**, unless a spec fixes its content. Mark approves each plan before its sub-issues are filed.
- **Commits:**
  - ask before committing, except inside a review loop;
  - use conventional commits;
  - no `Co-Authored-By` or other attribution lines. This overrides any harness default.
- **Push only with Mark's explicit OK.** If a push is rejected, stop and report it. Never `pull --rebase`, reset or force-push.
- **When running unattended,** turn an open question into a bead labelled `human` instead of blocking on it.

## Email and mailing lists

- **`fm`** is the Fastmail CLI for Mark's mail. Read with `fm search`, `fm email read` and `fm email thread`. Send with `fm draft new` or `fm draft reply`, then `fm draft send`. Mark's Fastmail is subscribed to the mimi and mls lists. Each send needs Mark's OK, like any other upstream post.
- **The IETF list archives** are on `imap.ietf.org:993` (TLS, read-only). Log in as `anonymous` with `mark@reviewcommit.com` as the password. We don't hide who is reading. Each list is a folder under `Shared Folders/`, for example `Shared Folders/mimi` and `Shared Folders/mls`.

## Build and test

Run everything before proposing a commit:

```bash
cargo fmt --all --check
typos
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo hack check --workspace --feature-powerset --depth 2 --no-dev-deps
RUSTDOCFLAGS="--cfg docsrs -D warnings" cargo +nightly doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features
cargo test --workspace --all-features
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same checks. There is no minimum supported Rust version: mimid supports only the latest stable.
